retained_knowledge.subject: the shape of the first language's own API: that a subscript on a document yields a collection, and that adding yields an object
retained_knowledge.reason: No library publishes its API shape as data, and inference over first-language source is the source server's whole job. The drift-prone half, the names of the entry points and the recognised types, is derived from the installed library by library_surface.py and is not written down. What remains is shape, not schema: no object type and no field name appears in that file, and tools/check_knowledge.py is what keeps that true.
retained_knowledge.tracked: Removing it would mean implementing a type checker, which is not smaller. Recorded in plan.md Complexity Tracking, and covered by tests that fail when the library renames the members involved.

retained_knowledge.subject: arithmetic over model text, converting the unit the language service states into the unit the protocol requires
retained_knowledge.reason: The protocol demands positions in a unit the language service does not speak, and feature 005 requires conversion to be possible without the service knowing a protocol exists, which places the conversion on this side by construction. It converts between text encodings, not between meanings: it needs no schema and no grammar.
retained_knowledge.tracked: Permanent by construction. Confined to one module, which tools/check_knowledge.py exempts by name and nothing else.

capabilities.reason: This server reads Python source. Classifying model text needs the IDF syntax layer, which lives in the language service and is reached from the second language, not from here. Installing this server with pip alone therefore yields no answers about model text, and no amount of work here would change that.
capabilities.instead: The model server, which serves model text and is bundled in the editor extension.
